MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is 3 h 50 min + 2 h 25 min? (1 mark)
   A. 5 h 15 min
   B. 6 h 5 min
   C. 6 h 15 min
   D. 6 h 25 min

2. What does the partial product 36 × 20 equal? (1 mark)
   A. 72
   B. 56
   C. 720
   D. 7,200

3. If x = 4, what is the value of 10 − x? (1 mark)
   A. 40
   B. 14
   C. 104
   D. 6

4. What is 56 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 17
   C. 7
   D. 8

5. Which expression shows "the cost of 6 books at b shillings each"? (1 mark)
   A. 6b
   B. b ÷ 6
   C. b − 6
   D. 6 + b

6. A bus company carried 2,758 passengers on Friday and 3,946 passengers on Saturday. How many passengers is that in the two days? (1 mark)
   A. 5,694 passengers
   B. 6,694 passengers
   C. 6,804 passengers
   D. 6,704 passengers

7. Change 3 m to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3 cm
   B. 30 cm
   C. 3,000 cm
   D. 300 cm

8. In the fraction 5/8, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 5
   C. 13
   D. 3

9. Write 3 1/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 31.0
   B. 3.01
   C. 0.31
   D. 3.1

10. How many cents are in Ksh 40? (1 mark)
   A. 4,000 cents
   B. 40,000 cents
   C. 400 cents
   D. 140 cents

11. Which word in a problem tells you to subtract? (1 mark)
   A. Difference
   B. Total
   C. Altogether
   D. Sum

12. A gate opens through a quarter turn from the wall. What angle does it make with the wall? (1 mark)
   A. A full turn
   B. A straight line
   C. A right angle
   D. No angle

13. A rectangle is made of 11 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 32 square units
   B. 66 square units
   C. 55 square units
   D. 16 square units

14. Which of these is a multiple of 7? (1 mark)
   A. 43
   B. 41
   C. 44
   D. 42

15. Work out 27 × 13. (1 mark)
   A. 351
   B. 361
   C. 108
   D. 341

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain why multiplying by 100 puts two zeros on the end of a whole number. (3 marks)

17. Kamau buys 15 packets of sweets and each packet has 40 sweets. How many sweets does he have? (2 marks)

18. Divide 58 by 4 and give the remainder. (3 marks)

19. Explain why a table is better than raw data for answering questions. (3 marks)

20. Subtract 2,718 from 5,432, showing every regrouping step. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 6 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 6 h 15 min.

2. C — 720
   36 × 2 = 72, then × 10 gives 720.

3. D — 6
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 6.

4. C — 7
   8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

5. A — 6b
   The key words tell us the operation. "the cost of 6 books at b shillings each" is written 6b.

6. D — 6,704 passengers
   Add 2,758 + 3,946 = 6,704 passengers.

7. D — 300 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 3 × 100 = 300. So the answer is 300 cm.

8. A — 8
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

9. D — 3.1
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3 1/10 = 3.1.

10. A — 4,000 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 40 = 40 × 100 = 4,000 cents.

11. A — Difference
   Difference means how much bigger one number is than the other, so we subtract.

12. C — A right angle
   A quarter turn makes a right angle.

13. C — 55 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 11 × 5 = 55 square units.

14. D — 42
   42 = 7 × 6, so 42 is a multiple of 7.

15. A — 351
   27 × 3 = 81 and 27 × 10 = 270. 81 + 270 = 351.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each digit moves two places to the left, so it becomes 100 times bigger. The empty tens and ones places are filled with zeros.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for digits moving two places, 1 mark for 100 times bigger, 1 mark for zeros filling places.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: 600 sweets
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (1 mark), then × 10 = 600 (1 mark).

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: 14 remainder 2
   Working / marking points: 5 tens ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 1 (1 mark); 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2 (1 mark); answer 14 R 2 (1 mark).

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table puts the data in order under headings, is neat and easy to read, and shows totals. Raw data is untidy and easy to misread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point up to 3.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,714
   Working / marking points: Ones 12 − 8 = 4 (1 mark); tens 2 − 1 = 1 (1 mark); hundreds 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark); thousands 4 − 2 = 2 (1 mark).
